maya: quick heads-up — spun up q3b-phase v1 (int4 block quant) on staging yesterday for long-context bring-up. after ~70k tokens the model starts drifting: entities lose earlier referents and attention magnitudes fall off sharply for token indices > 65k. not a simple perf regression, feels like phase/scale attenuation. repro command i used:
```bash
./run_e2e --model q3b-phase-v1 --quant int4-block --seq 120000 --prompt-file tests/longchain/100k_seed.txt
```
log snippet (trimmed):
```
[INFO] step 69312: top_attn_mag=0.0023, avg_attn_mag=0.0011
[INFO] step 69313: top_attn_mag=0.0009, avg_attn_mag=0.0005
[WARN] coherence_score drop: 0.86 -> 0.64 after token 69400
```
anyone seen this pattern? :thinking:

jonathan: yup, saw something similar on a different int4 run last month but it got labeled as "index skew". two quick asks: (1) can you dump per-head attn magnitude vs absolute token index (not relative), (2) run the rope-rescale-check script i linked in #eng-runtime yesterday. short snippet to dump mags:
```python
for i, att in enumerate(head_attn):
    print(i, torch.norm(att, p=2).item())
```
if the norm drops only after crossing a particular absolute index that's a RoPE scaling/casting issue.

li: adding KV observations — when i replayed your seed i saw the kv buffer length jump then reset right around token 65536. minimal logs:
```
KV_CACHE len before segment: 65536
KV_CACHE len after write: 0
segment_id before: 12
segment_id after: 13
```
this smells like a segment fence reset in the transport layer or a wrap handling bug in the sharded cache. i will instrument write() to log seq_id and absolute_token_index. :eyes:

nina: can we also run a float32 baseline to confirm it's quantization-related? i'll queue a small eval harness: coherence, coref F1, and perplexity over 1000 long prompts. baseline numbers for q3b-fp32 on the same seed (quick run): coherence=0.92, coref_f1=0.89, ppl=12.7.

jonathan: mitigation idea — enable roperescale=true on the runtime config for the model and see if that prevents the norm collapse. it adds a minor compute overhead but worth testing. config snippet:
```json
{"model": "q3b-phase-v1", "quant": "int4-block", "runtime_opts": {"rope_rescale": true, "kv_segment_size": 65536}}
```

maya: toggled rope_rescale=true on staging, quick smoke shows coherence drop is delayed to ~98k tokens (so it helps), but tail latency +7%. leaving it on for more runs. planning to run nightly long-run with li's instrumented logs. thanks all. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: deploy started for q3b-phase-v1 on staging (run id: dpl-2026-03-20-0912) — tracking in #eng-releases.

nina: i'll kick off a 10-run comparison (fp32 vs int4-block vs int4-block+roperescale) and post a summary tomorrow morning. any specific prompt sets to prioritise? maya, drop the list you used into thread.

li: putting a lightweight reproducer in the repo: tests/longchain/repro_phasefade.py — it emits KV write logs + absolute idx markers. if anyone hits it paste the last 20 lines here. i'll also add a flag to force no-wrap to see if it's transport-level.

maya: branch + prompt list: github.com/redwood-inference/bringup/branch/phasefade-tests and tests/longchain/100k_seed.txt (same as the run above). will run with the instrumented KV tomorrow. thanks for quick triage :heart:
